subject: Exhibit C — credit rebalance and packaging questions
messages:
From: Meredith Jones <mjones@polaris.so>

Cc: procurements@polaris.so
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit C — credit rebalance and packaging questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for sending the draft order form last week. Our procurement team reviewed Exhibit C (pricing schedule) and we have a few requests before legal will greenlight the SOW:

- Section 2(b): the minimum monthly commitment language still creates a clawback exposure in month 1 for our usage pattern. We'd like to propose a 60-day true-up instead of monthly.
- Section 3: the "safety net" credit calculation references a floor but doesn't clarify whether credits are applied pro rata across bundled SKUs. Could you confirm how credits flow to bundle components?
- Appendix A (fee bands): we'd like a one-time reallocation of 10% of the "overage" band to the base bucket for the first two quarters as a transitional concession.

I've attached a short workbook with our expected monthly curves and a redline request from our commercial counsel (high level). Can your team confirm whether these changes will require retiming of the committed pricing (and if so, a pricing impact estimate)?

We appreciate the flexibility — Polaris is excited to move forward but needs this spelled out for sign-off.

Thanks,
Meredith
Meredith Jones
Head of Procurement, Polaris Systems
Attachments: Polaris_Billing_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), Polaris_legal_comments.docx (document)

Hi Meredith — thanks for the clear notes and the workbook. Opening a quick thread internally and looping Karthik and Marissa so we can scope the legal redlines and product impact. Initial thoughts:

- 60-day true-up: that is reasonable operationally (we have prefix/KV cache considerations), but it changes the billing recognition window; Finance will want to confirm month of revenue recognition.
- Pro rata credit flow to bundled SKUs: product needs to confirm that credits can be allocated at SKU granularity versus only at invoice line level. That affects how the billing workbook maps to our invoice templates.
- One-time reallocation: this is a commercial concession we can likely grant for Q1–Q2, but it will reduce the "overage" band capacity for the period; we should quantify expected cost delta.

Karthik — can you and Legal draft a narrow Exhibit C redline that: 1) shifts true-up to 60 days, 2) clarifies "credit flow" language for bundled SKUs, and 3) adds a temporary reallocation clause that auto-reverts after two quarters? Put anything material to pricing in a separate pricing note so we can share numbers with Meredith.

Marissa — please estimate P&L impact for the two-quarter reallocation and whether we need to adjust commit bands. Meredith — once we have the redline + cushion estimate, we can present a single clean markup for sign-off.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit C — credit rebalance and packaging questions

Lauren / Marissa — drafting notes below that I will turn into a tracked PDF (Exhibit_C_v3_redline.pdf). Please flag anything you disagree with.

1) 60-day true-up (Section 2(b))
Proposed language (short): "Customer and Provider shall perform a usage true-up within sixty (60) calendar days following the end of each billing period. Any shortfall shall be invoiced or credited on the next invoice following the true-up period."
Comment: keeps mechanics simple, avoids monthly invoice churn, and aligns with our batching cadence. Finance note: will push invoicing of adjustments by up to ~30 days later.

2) Credit flow for bundles (Section 3 / Definitions)
Proposed language (short): "Credits issued under this Exhibit shall be applied at the invoice line level where practicable. Where a bundle maps to multiple invoice lines, credits will be allocated pro rata to bundle components based on recorded usage in the applicable period; if usage data is insufficient, credits shall first be applied to the Customer's base SKU charges."
Comment: explicit pro rata language mitigates ambiguity and matches Polaris' ask while protecting Redwood if usage telemetry is incomplete.

3) Temporary reallocation (Appendix A)
Proposed language: "Notwithstanding Section X, for the first sixty (60) days following the Effective Date, Provider shall reallocate up to ten percent (10%) of charges otherwise allocable to the 'Overage' band into the 'Base Commitment' band. This reallocation shall automatically revert at the start of the first calendar quarter following such sixty-day period unless otherwise agreed in writing."
Comment: I used 60 days per their Q1–Q2 ask to keep window explicit; counsel may prefer "first two calendar quarters" — open to modifying the trigger.

4) Audit / evidence box
Add a short clause allowing Redwood to request usage evidence within 30 days of applying credits if allocation is disputed. Keeps us able to validate pro rata allocations.

I'll generate the redline and include a separate pricing note with estimated delta.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit C — credit rebalance and packaging questions

Agree with Karthik's language; a few commercial clarifications from Product/Revenue: 

- For the 60-day true-up, recommend we make the invoicing window explicit: "adjustments will be billed on the invoice issued 30–75 days after period end" so Finance can map cash flows.
- On pro rata allocation: we can support per-SKU credits if Polaris provides SKU-level tags in their usage file. If not, we apply at invoice-line level which tends to allocate to higher-price SKUs first. We should include an "SKU tagging" definition and a simple onboarding checklist for Polaris to enable per-SKU allocation.
- On the 10% reallocation: Product suggests tying the concession to "first two invoice cycles" rather than calendar quarters to avoid ambiguity with billing cadence.

I'll run the numbers quickly and attach a short pricing note. If we go invoice-cycle based reversion (Product's preference), the cost delta for Redwood is roughly ~3.2% of committed revenue in Q1 (estimate attached).

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Product Revenue | Redwood Inference

Meredith — thanks for your patience. Attached is our tracked Exhibit C (Exhibit_C_v3_redline.pdf) and a brief pricing note explaining the expected P&L impact if Polaris elects the 10% transitional reallocation tied to "first two invoice cycles" (we used invoice-cycle reversion per Product's recommendation). Key callouts: 

- True-up: moved to 60 days, with explicit invoice timing: adjustments billed on the invoice issued between 30–75 days after period end.
- Credit allocation: clarified pro rata to SKU where Polaris provides SKU tags; otherwise credits will apply at invoice line level. We've included an onboarding checklist to enable SKU tagging.
- Transitional reallocation: language grants a one-time 10% reallocation from "Overage" to "Base Commitment" for the first two invoice cycles, with automatic reversion after the second invoice cycle.
- Audit clause: Redwood may request usage evidence within 30 days if a credit allocation is disputed.

Attachments: Exhibit_C_v3_redline.pdf (tracked redline), Polaris_Billing_Workbook.xlsx (we've annotated column mappings).

Can you confirm whether Polaris can supply SKU-level tags for usage records and whether the two-invoice-cycle reversion works operationally? If yes, we can package this into a clean order form and send a DocuSign link.

Best,
Lauren
